scenario.title: Late shipments
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

M-HANDOVER-LATE-RATE.name: Orders late at handover stage rate
M-HANDOVER-LATE-RATE.numerator: orders recorded late at handover stage

M-PICKUP-DELAY-DUR.name: Median delay between scheduled and actual carrier pickup

M-ORDERS-MISSED-PICKUP-COUNT.name: Orders released by warehouse only after carrier pickup already occurred

F-01.statement: Pickup-log data shows a median pickup delay of 2.0 hours across 60 recorded pickups.

F-02.statement: Order-db records show 300 of 1000 orders (30%) are late at the handover stage.

F-03.statement: WMS RELEASE-BATCH job failed in 21 of 30 runs (70%).

F-04.statement: 290 orders were released by the warehouse batch job only after the carrier pickup had already occurred.

F-05.statement: Carrier contract §3 requires SH-CAR confirmation before pickup schedule changes are run.

F-06.statement: Pickup-log slot-level data shows all 6 recorded slots (S-0 to S-5) have a delay_h of 2.0 hours, with no variation across slots.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

CL-02.statement: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

H-COMMUNICATION-GAP.statement: Parcels are being delayed for known/explainable reasons already captured somewhere, and customer dissatisfaction stems only from not being told why; a chatbot surfacing existing data resolves the issue.

H-WAREHOUSE-BACKLOG.statement: Lateness originates upstream in the shop's own warehouse processing (WMS job delays) before parcels ever reach the carrier handoff.

H-HANDOFF-BREAKDOWN.statement: Lateness is caused by failures in the Shop-to-Carrier handoff (H-PICK), e.g. pickup schedule changes not confirmed by the carrier.

H-CARRIER-TRANSIT-DELAY.statement: Parcels are picked up on schedule but delayed during carrier transit, i.e. the cause sits inside ORG-CAR's own operations after H-PICK completes.

H-DIAGNOSTIC-BLINDSPOT.statement: No single party currently has integrated visibility across orders, warehouse jobs, and pickup logs, so the true cause(s) of lateness are undiagnosed and vary case by case.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Pickup-log data shows a median delay of 2.0 hours across 60 pickups, indicating that the pickup event itself (handoff point H-PICK) is routinely delayed rather than occurring on schedule.

Order-db's stage breakdown shows 300 of 1000 orders (30%) are recorded as late specifically at the handover stage, confirming the handoff point as a measurable, quantified source of order-level lateness. The record covers only the handover stage, so it does not speak to how much lateness, if any, originates at other stages.

E-03.content: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-LOG (logistics lead, non-authoritative interview) claims the carrier's two-hour-late pickup is the cause of parcel lateness; the two-hour figure matches E-01's measured pickup delay, but the causal attribution itself remains an unverified stakeholder opinion, not new measured evidence.

The RELEASE-BATCH job failed in 21 of 30 runs and 290 orders were released by the warehouse only after carrier pickup had already occurred, pointing to a warehouse-side processing bottleneck that delays order readiness independent of the carrier's own pickup timing.

E-05.content: Carrier contract §3: pickup schedule changes run after SH-CAR confirms.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Carrier contract §3 establishes that pickup schedule changes execute only after SH-CAR confirms, matching the existing K-SCHED human-approval constraint on the push_pickup_schedule protected action; this is a governance/authority fact, not causal evidence about why parcels are late.

pickup-log's slot-level breakdown (E-06) shows all 6 recorded pickup slots (S-0 through S-5) have an identical delay_h of 2.0, matching E-01's measured median. The delay does not vary by scheduled slot, which is consistent with a single systemic cause (e.g. the warehouse release bottleneck, E-04) rather than slot-specific carrier transit variability.

U-OVERLAP-POPULATION.question: Do the 290 orders released after carrier pickup (E-04) overlap with the 300 orders recorded late at the handover stage (E-02), or are these distinct lateness populations?
U-OVERLAP-POPULATION.decision_impact: Determines whether fixing RELEASE-BATCH failures alone resolves most handover-stage lateness or only part of it.
U-OVERLAP-POPULATION.resolution_path: Join order-level identifiers/timestamps across DA-ORD and DA-WMS to measure the overlap between the two late populations.
U-OVERLAP-POPULATION.safe_placeholder: Treat WMS failures and handover lateness as two reported, possibly overlapping, contributing factors rather than a single confirmed cause until correlated.

U-WMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Is deeper diagnosis of RELEASE-BATCH failures currently blocked by the non-transient ACCESS_PENDING condition noted in the recovery log for wms-jobs?
U-WMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: If access remains blocked, further root-cause drill-down into why RELEASE-BATCH fails cannot proceed via the current tool surface.
U-WMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Escalate the ACCESS_PENDING condition for wms-jobs release_batch_runs and retry once resolved.
U-WMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Rely on the already-committed E-04 aggregate (21/30 failed runs, 290 orders) as the diagnostic baseline without deeper drill-down.

U-CARRIER-INDEPENDENT-DELAY.question: Does the carrier (ORG-CAR) contribute any independent delay beyond the warehouse-caused missed pickup window, given SH-LOG's carrier-fault claim (CL-02/E-03) is only non-authoritative stakeholder opinion?
U-CARRIER-INDEPENDENT-DELAY.decision_impact: Determines whether a carrier-facing fix such as a pickup schedule change is needed in addition to warehouse-side fixes.
U-CARRIER-INDEPENDENT-DELAY.resolution_path: Compare carrier arrival times against scheduled times independent of warehouse release timestamps.
U-CARRIER-INDEPENDENT-DELAY.safe_placeholder: Do not change the pickup schedule (protected action under K-SCHED) until any independent carrier-side contribution is confirmed.
U-CARRIER-INDEPENDENT-DELAY.resolution: E-06 shows no slot-to-slot variation (uniform 2.0h delay across S-0..S-5), weighing against a carrier-side independent delay that would be expected to vary by scheduled slot, though it does not conclusively rule out a constant carrier contribution.

A-WMS-HANDOVER-OVERLAP.statement: The 290 orders released after pickup (E-04) are assumed to substantially overlap with the 300 orders recorded late at the handover stage (E-02), rather than being two disjoint lateness causes.

A-PICKUP-DELAY-IS-DOWNSTREAM.statement: The 2-hour median pickup delay in pickup-log (E-01) is assumed to be a downstream effect of warehouse release failures (E-04) rather than independent carrier tardiness, consistent with the rejection of H-CARRIER-TRANSIT-DELAY.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.statement: The sampled 60 pickups, 1000 orders and 30 WMS runs are assumed representative of ongoing operations, since completeness of DA-PICK, DA-ORD and DA-WMS is marked UNKNOWN.

K-SCHED.description: pickup schedule changes need carrier confirmation

DA-PUSH-PICKUP-SCHEDULE.subject: ORG-CAR
conditions: Change must be confirmed by SH-CAR before it is run, per carrier contract §3.

SC-REDUCE-WMS-FAIL-RATE.statement: Reduce the WMS RELEASE-BATCH failed-run rate from its current 70% baseline so orders are released before scheduled carrier pickup.
SC-REDUCE-WMS-FAIL-RATE.validation_method: Re-query wms-jobs release_batch_runs after remediation and compare failed_runs/runs to the E-04 baseline.

SC-REDUCE-MISSED-PICKUP-COUNT.statement: Reduce the count of orders released only after carrier pickup already occurred below the current 290-order baseline.
SC-REDUCE-MISSED-PICKUP-COUNT.validation_method: Re-query wms-jobs release_batch_runs for orders_released_after_pickup and compare to baseline E-04.

SC-REDUCE-HANDOVER-LATE-RATE.statement: Reduce the proportion of orders recorded late at the handover stage below the current 30% baseline.
SC-REDUCE-HANDOVER-LATE-RATE.validation_method: Re-query order-db late_orders_by_stage for the handover stage and compare to baseline E-02.

VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION.unresolved_question: Do the 290 orders released after carrier pickup (E-04) overlap with the 300 orders recorded late at the handover stage (E-02), or are these distinct lateness populations?
VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Treat WMS failures and handover lateness as two reported, possibly overlapping, contributing factors rather than a single confirmed cause until correlated.
VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION.validation_method: Join order-level identifiers/timestamps across DA-ORD and DA-WMS to measure the overlap between the two late populations.

VOB-R-2.unresolved_question: Can the agent autonomously execute the WMS access grant (SR-R2) without a hidden approval requirement, given no HUMAN_APPROVAL constraint is recorded for WMS ownership/configuration changes?
VOB-R-2.reason_deferred: proposed by reasoner R-13: The feasibility step assumes this administrative action is unconstrained, but no stakeholder evidence confirms the absence of an unmodeled approval requirement, and acting incorrectly would create governance risk while diagnosis of the root-cause remedy (SR-R1) remains blocked.
VOB-R-2.validation_method: Confirm with SH-WMS or ORG-1 access policy whether an administrative WMS access grant requires sign-off beyond the K-SCHED-style constraints already modeled.
required_evidence: Explicit confirmation from SH-WMS on access-grant authority

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CX requests a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late (CL-01, initial_request).
symptoms: Customers receive no explanation for parcel lateness, prompting the chatbot request (CL-01).
30% of orders are recorded late specifically at the handover stage (E-02/F-02).
Median carrier pickup occurs 2.0 hours after schedule across 60 pickups (E-01/F-01).
WMS RELEASE-BATCH job fails in 21 of 30 runs, with 290 orders released only after pickup already occurred (E-04/F-03/F-04).
problem_definition.root_problem: Parcels are delivered late because the warehouse's RELEASE-BATCH job fails in 70% of its runs (21/30, E-04), causing 290 orders to be released only after the carrier's scheduled pickup had already occurred; these orders surface as the 30% of orders recorded late at the Shop-to-Carrier handover stage (E-02), and the resulting missed pickup windows produce the 2.0-hour median pickup delay in the pickup-log (E-01) — not tardiness by the carrier itself (H-CARRIER-TRANSIT-DELAY is rejected by E-01, E-03, E-04).

trace.summary: Parcels are delivered late because the warehouse's RELEASE-BATCH job fails in 70% of its runs (21/30, E-04), causing 290 orders to be released only after the carrier's scheduled pickup had already occurred; these orders surface as the 30% of orders recorded late at the Shop-to-Carrier handover stage (E-02), and the resulting missed pickup windows produce the 2.0-hour median pickup delay in the pickup-log (E-01) — not tardiness by the carrier itself (H-CARRIER-TRANSIT-DELAY is rejected by E-01, E-03, E-04).

structural_remedies.description: Repair/reconfigure the RELEASE-BATCH WMS job (owned by ORG-1/SH-WMS) to eliminate the 70% failure rate so orders release before carrier pickup.
structural_remedies.rationale: No HUMAN_APPROVAL constraint governs WMS job configuration (K-SCHED only covers push_pickup_schedule), but the recovery log shows diagnosis is currently halted by a NOT_TRANSIENT ACCESS_PENDING condition with no fallback, so the technical fix cannot proceed yet within remaining budget_remaining_minutes=225.; residual gap: Even if access were restored, the specific technical defect causing failed runs is still undiagnosed; SC-REDUCE-WMS-FAIL-RATE cannot be confirmed met without that diagnosis.

structural_remedies.description: Grant/restore the pending WMS access (ownership/configuration fix) that is blocking deeper RELEASE-BATCH failure diagnosis per U-WMS-ACCESS-PENDING.
structural_remedies.rationale: wms-jobs tool_health is HEALTHY and no HUMAN_APPROVAL constraint restricts read diagnosis of DA-WMS; an ownership-level access grant is an administrative action with no stated approval gate.; residual gap: Restoring access only unblocks diagnosis; it does not by itself fix the job failures (R1 still required).

structural_remedies.description: As an interim process change, shift the WMS release job's run window earlier relative to the carrier's scheduled pickup time so orders are more likely released before pickup even while failures persist.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is purely an ORG-1 internal scheduling change to the WMS job (not push_pickup_schedule), so K-SCHED's carrier-approval requirement does not apply.; residual gap: Does not reduce the 70% RELEASE-BATCH failure rate itself, so M-WMS-FAIL-RATE and SC-REDUCE-WMS-FAIL-RATE remain unmet; only mitigates M-ORDERS-MISSED-PICKUP-COUNT symptomatically.

structural_remedies.description: Run the already-scoped correlate_wms_releases_with_handover_lateness query joining DA-WMS and DA-ORD to resolve VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION before any remedy is treated as fixing handover lateness.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a read-only correlation against order-db and wms-jobs, both HEALTHY, with no protected-action or approval constraint attached to this scope item.; residual gap: Confirms or disconfirms the A-WMS-HANDOVER-OVERLAP assumption but does not itself reduce WMS failures or pickup delay; VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION remains BEFORE_RELEASE-blocking until resolved.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: WMS RELEASE-BATCH job fails in 21 of 30 runs (70%), E-04/F-03. → 290 orders are consequently released by the warehouse only after the carrier's scheduled pickup has already occurred, E-04/F-04. → These missed-pickup orders surface as late at the Shop-to-Carrier handover stage H-PICK, matching the 30% handover-late rate in order-db, E-02/F-02. → The resulting missed pickup windows produce the 2.0-hour median pickup delay recorded in the pickup-log, E-01/F-01, rather than carrier-side tardiness (H-CARRIER-TRANSIT-DELAY rejected by E-01,E-03,E-04). → Parcels reach customers late without any stated reason, generating the complaint behind the chatbot request, CL-01.; rejected framings: [('H-CARRIER-TRANSIT-DELAY', 'Explicitly REJECTED in state; contradicted by E-01, E-03 and E-04, which trace the delay to warehouse release timing rather than carrier transit.'), ('H-COMMUNICATION-GAP', "Only a CANDIDATE with no supporting evidence; it mirrors the requester's chatbot framing (CL-01) and would leave the WMS/handoff failure mechanism unaddressed."), ('CL-02 (carrier-fault attribution)', "SH-LOG's claim is non-authoritative stakeholder opinion (E-03); E-04 shows the delay pattern traces to warehouse release failures, not carrier tardiness, even though the 2h magnitude matches E-01."), ('H-DIAGNOSTIC-BLINDSPOT', 'Candidate with no direct supporting evidence; the committed data (E-01, E-02, E-04) already identifies a specific, measurable mechanism, so lateness is not purely undiagnosed or case-by-case.')]
[CONDITIONAL] handoff H-PICK delivery/semantic validity unknown; [CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-OVERLAP-POPULATION deferred to VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION

framing_assertion.rationale: The initial request (SH-CX) asks only to build a chatbot explaining lateness, implicitly asserting the root problem is lack of customer-facing explanation rather than an unresolved operational delay in P-SHIP.

hypotheses.statement: Parcels are being delayed for known/explainable reasons already captured somewhere, and customer dissatisfaction stems only from not being told why; a chatbot surfacing existing data resolves the issue.
hypotheses.rationale: This is SH-CX's framing: it assumes causes are already determinable from existing records and only communication is missing, so the fix is a read-only Q&A layer with no process change to P-SHIP or H-PICK.

hypotheses.statement: Lateness originates upstream in the shop's own warehouse processing (WMS job delays) before parcels ever reach the carrier handoff.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, the fix is an internal warehouse-process intervention (e.g. via SH-WMS/SH-LOG) rather than a chatbot, since the delay is created inside ORG-1 before H-PICK occurs.
discriminating_evidence: P-SHIP process steps field is currently empty, so warehouse timing is unverified

hypotheses.statement: Lateness is caused by failures in the Shop-to-Carrier handoff (H-PICK), e.g. pickup schedule changes not confirmed by the carrier.
hypotheses.rationale: The handoff H-PICK has UNKNOWN delivery_status and semantic_validity, and K-SCHED requires carrier confirmation for pickup schedule changes; a breakdown here would require fixing the approval/confirmation loop, not just explaining delays.

hypotheses.statement: Parcels are picked up on schedule but delayed during carrier transit, i.e. the cause sits inside ORG-CAR's own operations after H-PICK completes.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, the shop (ORG-1) cannot fix the root cause itself; the chatbot could only report carrier-caused delays, and resolution authority shifts to SH-CAR/ORG-CAR.

actions.question: Which pipeline stage (warehouse processing, carrier pickup, carrier transit) are late orders currently stuck at, according to order-db records?
actions.expected_information_gain: Reveals which pipeline stage accumulates delay, directly separating warehouse, handoff, and carrier-transit hypotheses.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: Determines whether the next investigation/mitigation effort should target warehouse ops, the handoff process, or the carrier.
actions.why_now: No stage-level late-order data has yet been queried; it is a prerequisite before deciding where mitigation effort should focus.

actions.question: Does the pickup log show parcels picked up on time but still arriving late, or were the pickups themselves delayed?
actions.expected_information_gain: Clarifies whether delay originates in the Shop-to-Carrier handoff (H-PICK) or after pickup inside carrier transit.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: Determines whether remediation should target handoff confirmation (constrained by K-SCHED approval) or carrier-side transit operations, which have different owners.
actions.why_now: H-PICK handoff delivery_status and semantic_validity are currently UNKNOWN and form the key fork between handoff-breakdown and carrier-transit hypotheses.

actions.question: Do warehouse release batch run logs show processing delays before parcels reach the carrier handoff?
actions.expected_information_gain: Determines whether upstream warehouse batch-release timing contributes to lateness, confirming or ruling out the warehouse-backlog hypothesis.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If warehouse releases run on schedule, upstream fix effort can be de-prioritized in favor of handoff/carrier investigation.
actions.why_now: Warehouse job completeness is UNKNOWN and no warehouse-side data has yet been checked for this stage of the pipeline.

actions.question: From the logistics lead's perspective, which handoffs or systems lack integrated visibility into why parcels are late, and is the cause already known somewhere?
actions.expected_information_gain: Surfaces whether an integrated diagnosis already exists (supporting the communication-gap hypothesis) or confirms a cross-system blind spot (diagnostic-blindspot hypothesis).

proposal.summary:
The customer-experience team (SH-CX) asked for a chatbot to explain late parcels (CL-01), but investigation of order-db, pickup-log and wms-jobs data traced the actual root cause to the warehouse's RELEASE-BATCH job: it fails in 21 of 30 runs (70%, E-04), causing 290 orders to be released only after carrier pickup already happened; these appear as the 300/1000 orders (30%) recorded late at handover (E-02) and as the 2.0-hour median pickup delay seen in 60 pickup-log records, uniform across all 6 pickup slots (E-01, E-06). The DEFINE gate for this problem definition returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring one high-impact open question (VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION) rather than blocking entirely. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: only the narrow, already-verified scope item "verify_pickup_window_alignment" against the pickup-log data (DA-PICK) was released (work item W-WI-01, DONE), while the actual WMS repair and other scoped actions (diagnosing RELEASE-BATCH, correlating WMS releases with handover lateness, adjusting the carrier pickup schedule) remain unfinished and outside release scope.</summary>
<key_points">[]</key_points>
key_points: Stakeholder SH-CX's chatbot request (CL-01) was a hypothesis to test, not the confirmed problem; the carrier-fault claim from SH-LOG (CL-02/E-03) was non-authoritative stakeholder opinion.
The hypothesis that carrier transit (not warehouse release) causes delay, H-CARRIER-TRANSIT-DELAY, was REJECTED, contradicted by E-01, E-03, E-04 and E-06.
Two supported hypotheses converge on the warehouse: H-WAREHOUSE-BACKLOG (supported by E-04, E-06) and H-HANDOFF-BREAKDOWN (supported by E-01, E-02, E-03, E-04, E-06).

The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS: handoff H-PICK delivery/semantic validity is unknown, and the critical unknown U-OVERLAP-POPULATION was deferred rather than resolved, tracked as VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION.

Only the minimum useful scope item, verify_pickup_window_alignment against DA-PICK, was actually released (SD-1 release_scope, work item W-WI-01 marked DONE); the WMS-fix remedy (SR-R1) was assessed as not feasible in contest time.
No hold was placed on release despite open VOBs because their blocking_scope (diagnose_release_batch_job_failures and correlate_wms_releases_with_handover_lateness) falls outside the released scope.
Success criteria (SC-REDUCE-WMS-FAIL-RATE, SC-REDUCE-MISSED-PICKUP-COUNT, SC-REDUCE-HANDOVER-LATE-RATE) remain unmet since the WMS job fix itself was not executed.
limitations_explained: It has not yet been established whether the 290 orders released after pickup (E-04) and the 300 orders recorded late at handover (E-02) are the same orders, so any future improvement in the handover-late metric cannot yet be fully credited to a WMS fix (tracked as VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION / assumption A-WMS-HANDOVER-OVERLAP).
Deeper diagnosis of why the RELEASE-BATCH job fails 70% of the time is currently halted by a non-transient ACCESS_PENDING condition with no known workaround.
VOB-U-OVERLAP-POPULATION and VOB-R-2 remain OPEN; both are flagged as blocking the diagnose and correlate actions, so those actions were not performed as part of this release.
The quality of handoff H-PICK (delivery_status and semantic_validity) is UNKNOWN, which limits how much confidence can be placed in the pickup-window verification that was released.

Whether the sampled data (60 pickups, 1000 orders, 30 WMS runs) represents ongoing operations is unverified, because completeness of the underlying data assets DA-PICK, DA-ORD and DA-WMS is marked UNKNOWN (assumption A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS).
No remedy was pursued for adjusting the carrier pickup schedule, since the evidence points to a warehouse-side (not carrier) root cause and the pickup-sched tool's health status is UNKNOWN.
The actual fix for the RELEASE-BATCH job (owned by ORG-1/SH-WMS) was not completed in this release; it was judged not feasible within the available contest time.
